productArtifacts.title: Datastreamer for sensor and anomaly metrics
productArtifacts.body:
In Splunk OT Intelligence, open Data Ingestion and create a Datastreamer:
HEC hostname: the HTTP Event Collector URL of your Splunk platform deployment
HEC token: a token whose allowed indexes include the index below
Name: sensors & anomalies
Index: edge_hub_data (metrics index; name suffixed with _data)
Topics: edgehub/+/+/values, edgehub/+/+/anomalies
Data Volume: High
Backlog Size: 3,000,000
Batch Size: 10 or 25
Source Type: log2metrics_json

In the Splunk Edge mobile app, turn on anomaly detection for the accelerometer sensor. Anomaly metrics land in the same edge_hub_data index with type=anomaly-detector; the kNN model needs about a day of training data first.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `edge_hub_data` (UC-14.3.2)** — Planned work for 'Vibration & Motion Monitoring' shifts `count` over `span=1h` while `extracted_host` remains in-scope.  Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `count` on `configured_sourcetype`** — Scheduled automation elevates `src` without crossing `count` > 0 for UC-14.3.2. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `extracted_host`** — Health checks in `edge_hub_data` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `configured_sourcetype`** — First 48h baseline for UC-14.3.2 on `extracted_host` is unstable; window via `ops_exception_register.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` keyed on `extracted_host`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Splunk Edge Hub (built-in sensors), Splunk OT Intelligence.
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `index=edge_hub_data` (metrics index, `sourcetype=log2metrics_json`) — built-in 3-axis accelerometer + 6-axis gyroscope; anomaly metrics carry type=anomaly-detector. Sent to HEC by a Splunk Edge Hub OS Datastreamer configured in Splunk OT Intelligence (Edge Hub OS does not support a universal forwarder).
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Mount Edge Hub near rotating equipment (IP66 enclosure suits industrial environments, operating -40°C to 80°C). The built-in accelerometer and gyroscope stream metrics to `edge_hub_data`. Enable kNN anomaly detection via the mobile app for each axis. Deploy MLTK Smart Outlier Detection model for more advanced analysis (requires OT Intelligence 4.8.0+ and Edge Hub OS 2.0+). Alert on anomaly detections. Note: one ML model per sensor; performance degrades with 2+ concurrent models.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
| mstats count where index=edge_hub_data AND metric_name="accelerometer*" AND type="anomaly-detector"
  span=1h by extracted_host
| where count > 0
```

Understanding this SPL

**Vibration & Motion Monitoring** — Equipment vibration changes indicate bearing wear, misalignment, or imbalance. Edge Hub's built-in 3-axis accelerometer and gyroscope enable predictive maintenance without external sensors.

Documented **Data sources**: `index=edge_hub_data` (metrics index, `sourcetype=log2metrics_json`) — built-in 3-axis accelerometer + 6-axis gyroscope; anomaly metrics carry type=anomaly-detector. Sent to HEC by a Splunk Edge Hub OS Datastreamer configured in Splunk OT Intelligence (Edge Hub OS does not support a universal forwarder). **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Splunk Edge Hub (built-in sensors), Splunk OT Intelligence. The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: edge_hub_data.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Uses `mstats` to query metrics indexes (pre-aggregated metric data).
• Filters the current rows with `where count > 0` — typically the threshold or rule expression for this monitoring goal.

Note: for mstats, confirm the metrics indexes in the search exist and your role can run mstats. This is separate from CIM data model acceleration.

Step 3 — Validate
Confirm metric or event volume in the time range, then compare trends and device status to the Splunk Edge Hub admin UI or the mobile app for the same devices. Verify metric names, hosts, and time skew.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Line chart (accelerometer axes over time), Single value (current RMS), Timeline (anomaly events).

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Splunk Edge Hub (built-in sensors), Splunk OT Intelligence). Configure the Edge Hub Datastreamer and HEC token that write into edge_hub_data. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`extracted_host`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify the Datastreamer in Splunk OT Intelligence, the HEC token's allowed indexes, and HEC errors in `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd component=HttpInputDataHandler`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: We watch what edge sensors report from the physical world. We help you know if something is off with shaking that might mean a bearing, balance, or mount problem before harm, damage, or wasted effort piles up.
